solution: Summing over circular arrangements is the same as summing over all n! permutations and dividing by n. Expanding the product of (a_u + a_v) over the cycle makes every edge pick one of its two endpoints, so a term equals the product of a_v^{e_v} with e_v in {0,1,2} and sum of e_v equal to n; around the circle the vertices with e=2 (both edges pointing in) and those with e=0 must alternate, and once their positions are fixed the edge choices are forced, so a fixed pair of disjoint k-sets A (exponent 2) and B (exponent 0) is realised by exactly 2*C(n,2k)*(k!)^2*(n-2k)!/n = 2(n-1)!/C(2k,k) arrangements, giving answer = 2(n-1)! * sum_k W_k / C(2k,k) where W_k = sum over such A,B of (prod_A a^2)(prod of the remaining a). The weights W_k are obtained from the identity sum_k W_k (t(1-t))^k = [z^n] prod_i (1 + t a_i z)(1 + (1-t) a_i z) = sum_j e_j e_{n-j} t^j (1-t)^{n-j}, where e is the elementary symmetric polynomial sequence of a, built by a divide-and-conquer NTT product tree; one convolution turns that into the coefficients of H(t), a Taylor shift t -> 1/2 + s makes H even in s, and a final binomial transform in y = s^2 with r = 1/4 - y reads off every W_k. Total cost O(n log^2 n), dominated by the product tree, everything modulo 998244353. The derivation was checked against a brute force over all (n-1)! arrangements on random n <= 7 and reproduces all three sample answers 120, 12 and 265885269.

notes: Solution fully derived and verified: a brute force over all (n-1)! circular arrangements agrees with the closed form on 60 random cases with n in 3..7 (small values and full mod-range values), the intermediate W_k values match a 3^n brute force, and all three official samples reproduce. Vocabulary gaps: the central objects here are generating functions, elementary symmetric polynomials, and a polynomial Taylor shift / binomial transform, and none of those has a slug in vocab.txt; 'fft' and 'combinatorics' are the closest real labels. 'divide-and-conquer' refers specifically to the D&C-with-NTT product tree that builds the elementary symmetric polynomials in O(n log^2 n) - it is genuinely required, since the naive O(n^2) computation of e_j is too slow at n = 2*10^5. Deliberately NOT labelled burnside-lemma: rotations are quotiented out by a plain division by n (all labels distinct), not by a group-action count.
